response:
I definitely lean toward deep, focused dives over rapid topic-hopping. 

When you jump between a dozen subjects, you only ever skim the surface—it’s easy to exchange trivia or quick takes, but you don't really get to unpack the nuance, challenge assumptions, or see how the other person truly thinks. Staying with one idea allows the conversation to breathe and develop its own momentum, peeling back layers until you reach something genuinely interesting or unexpected.

That said, I don't mind an organic tangent if it naturally connects back to the core thought. But if I have to choose between breadth and depth, depth wins every time. What about you? Do you thrive on variety, or do you like staying in one groove?
